Prebuilt **Linux and Windows x86-64** binaries of `k3`, the pure-C Kimi K3 inference
engine from [FareedKhan-dev/kimi-k3-in-c](https://github.com/FareedKhan-dev/kimi-k3-in-c),
built with the Tiny C Compiler (TCC) only.

**This release makes the TCC build faster again:**

- the matrix kernels are about 1.3x faster than in
  [v1.2.1](https://github.com/s81/kimi-work-8Gb/releases/tag/v1.2.1);
- the KDA recurrence step is 2.1x faster.

The output is bit-identical to v1.2.1 and every earlier build. Features, downloads and
system requirements are unchanged. If you use v1.2.0 or v1.2.1, upgrade.

## What changed

TCC keeps a value in a CPU register only within a single expression. Between
statements, it stores the value to memory and loads it back.

- **Chained additions.** Each accumulator's next additions in the bf16, fp32 and MXFP4
  kernels are now written as one expression, `a0 = a0 + e0 + e16 + ...`. C evaluates `+`
  left to right, so this performs the same additions in the same order as separate
  `a0 += e` statements, and gives the same bits.
- **KDA step.** The KDA recurrence step works through each row eight elements at a
  time. `k[i] * beta` and `v - u`, which the loops recalculated for every element, are
  now computed once; they are the same float values.
- **Left as they are.** SiTU-GLU, ShortConv and the KDA decay spend their time in the C
  library's `expf` and `tanhf`. Replacing those calls would change the results.
  Together with rmsnorm they take about 0.2 s per token on one core, against tens of
  seconds for the matrix kernels.

## Performance

Kernel benchmark on a 4-core Xeon at real Kimi K3 dimensions. Single timings on this
machine vary by up to 60%, so each figure is the best of 12 runs, measured back to back
against v1.2.1:

| Kernel | Threads | v1.2.1 | v1.2.2 | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| bf16 matmul 12288 x 7168 | 1 | 88.5 ms | 68.0 ms | 1.30x |
| bf16 matmul 12288 x 7168 | 4 | 24.0 ms | 17.5 ms | 1.37x |
| MXFP4 matmul 3072 x 3584 | 1 | 13.2 ms | 10.2 ms | 1.29x |
| MXFP4 matmul 3072 x 3584 | 4 | 3.67 ms | 2.85 ms | 1.29x |
| KDA step 128 x 128 | 1 | ~103 us | ~48 us | 2.1x |

- **Against v1.2.0:** the matrix kernels are now about 8-10x faster.
- **Against GCC:** the gap to the old GCC AVX2 build
  ([v1.1.0-win.1](https://github.com/s81/kimi-work-8Gb/releases/tag/v1.1.0-win.1)) is
  roughly 2x on bf16 and 2-3x on MXFP4. Treat this as approximate: the GCC figures are
  single runs from an earlier session.
- **Real inference:** a full model run gains less than these kernel figures wherever
  reading weights from disk dominates, as it does on the low-memory presets.

## Downloads

| File | Runs on |
|---|---|
| `k3-1.2.2-windows-x64.zip` | 64-bit Windows Vista or later, any x86-64 CPU |
| `k3-1.2.2-linux-x64.zip` | 64-bit Linux with glibc 2.38 or newer (e.g. Ubuntu 24.04, Debian 13, Fedora 39), any x86-64 CPU |
| `SHA256SUMS.txt` | Checksums for both zips |

Each zip contains `k3` (`k3.exe` on Windows), `LICENSE`, `NOTICE` and `README.txt`.

- **No installer and no extra DLLs.**
  - `k3.exe` imports only `kernel32.dll` and `msvcrt.dll`.
  - The Linux `k3` needs only `libc.so.6` and `libm.so.6`.
- **Verify the download.**
  - PowerShell: `Get-FileHash .\k3-1.2.2-windows-x64.zip -Algorithm SHA256`
  - Linux: `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS.txt --ignore-missing`
- **Quick check:** `k3 --version` should print `k3 1.2.2`.

Running inference needs the Kimi K3 checkpoint (about 1.56 TB), downloaded separately.
See [docs/QUICKSTART.md](https://github.com/s81/kimi-work-8Gb/blob/v1.2.2/docs/QUICKSTART.md).

## How it was built and verified

- **Build:** [`release.yml`](https://github.com/s81/kimi-work-8Gb/blob/v1.2.2/.github/workflows/release.yml)
  on GitHub's `ubuntu-latest` and `windows-latest` runners, with TCC 0.9.28rc (TinyCC
  commit `e23dabed`).
- **Test suite:** the full weightless suite ran on each OS before packaging, with these
  results: `22 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped`, `VERDICT: ENGINE MATCHES THE REFERENCE
  EXACTLY` and `ALL WEIGHTLESS TESTS PASSED`.
- **Same output as v1.2.1:** the new kernels were checked bit for bit against the
  v1.2.1 kernels on 206 cases, at 1 and 4 threads.
  - Sizes: odd lengths from 1 to 7168, and every MXFP4 group size.
  - Special values: NaN, infinity and 1e30, NaN scale bytes, and zero keys.
  - The benchmark output digests are unchanged.
- **Not verified:** inference on real Kimi K3 weights with the TCC build, and tokenizer
  parity. Both need the checkpoint, which CI does not have.

Full history: [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/s81/kimi-work-8Gb/blob/v1.2.2/CHANGELOG.md).
